text:
For **weekend tent camping**, I’d pick the **[BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 + 100W solar panel kit](https://dealectric.com/best-solar-generator-kit-for-tent-camping)**. It’s a more tent-friendly size than the big backup-style kits, and its **288Wh battery and 600W inverter** should cover phones, lights, and other modest camp electronics. The guide lists it at about **$490** and estimates roughly **four hours of good sun** to refill the battery.

The trade-off is limited capacity: it’s not the choice for running a fridge or lots of high-draw gear. If you want substantially more reserve, consider the **[Jackery Solar Generator 1000 v2 with a 200W panel](https://www.newworldsurvival.com/reviews/solar-generator-kit.html)** instead; it has **1,070Wh**, but is heavier and costs more. Either way, solar charging works best with the panel in open sun—shade and clouds can slow it considerably.

judge.top_pick: BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 + 100 W Solar Panel Kit
